stabilize_rounds.cause: Unbounded chat-folder leak (open issue #1309 — dead FOLDER_MENU_DELETE_ITEM testid) makes every create/rename's RTK-Query folder-list refetch an increasingly fragile network call; both specs in this file trigger it every run
stabilize_rounds.fix_summary: ChatPage.delete_folder_via_menu() now falls back to a new delete_folder_via_api() when the dead FOLDER_MENU_DELETE_ITEM testid prevents the dot-menu delete from locating its target, instead of silently swallowing the timeout and leaking the folder. Verified via independent ground truth (fresh page reload + raw API GET), not just 'no exception raised'. Added regression test TestChatFolderDeleteApiFallbackRegression::test_delete_folder_via_api_actually_removes_the_folder. Root cause (#1309, the dead testid) stays open/tracked — this is the test-side mitigation for the leak class it produces, not a mask.

cases.note: extend-existing against the merged ELITEA-2458 covering spec. Reviewer APPROVED after 1 fix round (third no-op signal + Coverage Map row-1 correction). Hardening gate went red non-deterministically on the pre-existing ELITEA-2458 test (unrelated to this case's own new scenarios); batch-stabilize diagnosed + fixed the real cause (test-data leak, #1309) in round 1; re-gate 3/3 green. Merged to automation/base via PR #1313 (squash, 5cc8647c).

findings.note: Reconfirmed live during analysis: EliteaAI/elitea-testing-public#1309 (chat-folder-menu-delete-menuitem regression) is still present/unresolved on main/automation/testids — document.querySelector for that testid returns null even though the visible Delete menuitem + confirmation dialog still function by text/role. Not fixed here (out of this case's own scope); it IS what caused the gate's red (see below) and now has a test-side mitigation (not a product fix).

#1309 (dead chat-folder dot-menu Delete testid) is confirmed to be actively accelerating shared-DEV-project data pollution: 19+ leaked chat folders as of 2026-08-07, and every run of this file's tests (both the pre-existing ELITEA-2458 test and this batch's new one) added 2 more permanently-orphaned folders every single hardening-gate re-run before the stabilize fix landed. This batch added a test-side leak-stopper (API-delete fallback) but the underlying UI regression is still open and still needs a human/product fix.

Assertion-strength regression from established in-file precedent, caught and fixed in fix round 1: the covering ELITEA-2458 test's own no-op-click check uses THREE independent signals (editor stays open + input value unchanged + no PUT fires), with 'editor stays open' as a compound check including chat.get_folder_item(folder_id).count()==0. The first implementation of this case's two new scenarios only used two signals. Fixed: third signal added to both new no-op-click blocks.

AFS extend-existing Axis-2 'signal parity' claims should be verified by diffing the actual assertion lists against the covering spec, not by matching prose — this round's gap slipped through because the description text was copied faithfully while one assertion was dropped. Durable memory entry written by the implementer: afs_signal_parity_claim_needs_assertion_diff.md.
Mechanical testid-only-locator grep on the full diff (both build and stabilize rounds, automation/ paths) returned 0 hits — no non-testid handle introduced.

reports/archive shows this same covering test also failed earlier the same session (00:07:00, single-spec run, before this batch's second test existed) with a different symptom — a 10s timeout waiting for a folder item to render after creation. Independent corroboration that this shared DEV project's folder-list read/render timing is already somewhat unstable; worth tracking if it recurs in a future batch.
